# E0512: effect that reaches `main`

A user-defined effect is handled before `main`, a test or an example ends. Wrap the code in `with (handler …) { … }`.

- Rule: [`handlers.no-effect-reaches-main`](../../reference/12-effects.md#handlers.no-effect-reaches-main)
- Reported at: the effect in the row, or the first performance outside every `with` of its effect.
- Tier: `advanced`, checked in the `types` phase

## Example

This program makes the mistake:

```stilt E0512:6
effect Log {
  fn log(msg: str)
}

fn main() / io {
  Log.log("start")
}
```

This one is fixed:

```stilt
effect Log {
  fn log(msg: str)
}

fn main() / io {
  with (handler Log { fn log(msg: str) { print(msg) } }) { Log.log("start") }
}
```

## What the compiler prints

`stilt check` on [`E0512_effect_that_reaches_main.lt`](../../tests/diagnostics/E0512_effect_that_reaches_main.lt):

```text
── EFFECT THAT REACHES `main` ─── E0512_effect_that_reaches_main.lt:6:3  [E0512]

This performs `Log`, but no `with` around it handles `Log`; wrap it in one:
`with h { … }`:

  6 │   Log.log("start")
    │   ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

A user-defined effect is handled before `main`, a test or an example ends. Wrap
the code in `with (handler …) { … }`.
```
